title: The tzimtzum and the reshimu: the teacher's one point, the soul in the body, the blueprint and the thrown stone
overview:
Chapter 12 explains the first *tzimtzum*, the first that relates to our *hishtalshelus*, and the *reshimu* left after it. They must be understood in detail and felt, because that is the key to true unity with *Atzmus Ein Sof*: seeing that everything, even the highest revelations and *Moshiach* itself, is like nothing before Him, a check to be cashed, so that a person wants only G-d Himself.

All the *meshalim* of the *tzimtzum* come to one point: the light is hidden in itself so that a little can shine. A teacher boils a deep idea down to one point for a small student, yet forgets nothing, and the short way holds it all, as the *Mishna* holds the *Gemara*. The soul holds back to live in a body, yet feels everything the body feels and loses nothing when a limb is lost.

The *reshimu* is an impression: nothing of the original is left, yet all of it can be drawn out. A blueprint, a mnemonic, a thrown stone, a hand sign and the moving fingers of a writer each hide it more, and the last points ahead to the *Kav*.

terms.gloss: contraction: the light hidden in itself so that only a little shines; not literal, since nothing is missing
an impression: the original is completely gone, not a residue, yet what was there can be figured out and drawn out of it
self-sacrifice: giving up anything, physical or even spiritual, to connect to G-d Himself
the days of old: here the middos as they are preceded in the essence before the tzimtzum, which is not bound by them
a vessel for a vessel: revealed not directly but indirectly, like an engraving in a diamond pressed into wax
He engraved an engraving: a double engraving, the letters estimated in Kadmon
the whole debate and reasoning behind a ruling, which the one who says it short still knows
the short way: the summary or the Mishna's short din, which includes all the length
the receiver; the student who is not comparable to the teacher
the form of man: the soul's spiritual form, hovering over the body and making it go the way it should
an impression or mark; here the craftsman's blueprint, a shorthand from which the whole building can be made

sections.title: Why the tzimtzum must be understood in depth: before Him everything is as nothing
sections.summary: The first *tzimtzum* and its *reshimu* look simple, but they have many details and must be felt, not only understood, because they are the key to unity with *Atzmus Ein Sof*: seeing that everything, even the whole *hishtalshelus* and the revelations of *Moshiach*, is like nothing before Him.

phrases.en: And now, we have to understand
the idea of this first *tzimtzum*.
as well as the *reshimu* that is left, the impression that's left after this first *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: **And now, we have to understand the idea of this first tzimtzum** (contraction). We are going to give a *mashal* (analogy) for it now. And with it, **the reshimu that is left**: the impression that is left after this first *tzimtzum*.

Really, this *tzimtzum* is not the first *tzimtzum*. There are *tzimtzumim* before it: there is a *tzimtzum* between *Echad* (one) and *Kadmon* (preceding), between *Yachid* (singular) and *Echad*, and between the *etzem* (essence) and *Yachid*. There is even a *tzimtzum* to get to the whole idea of an *etzem* and its revelations: even before the idea of *Atzmus* (G-d's essence), there is a *tzimtzum* from G-d Himself to get to the idea of *Atzmus*.

All the *tzimtzumim* that happened before this one are not called the first *tzimtzum*, because they do not relate directly to our *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent). This one is called the first because it is the first main *tzimtzum* that relates to our *hishtalshelus*.

phrases.en: even though that is known to people that are familiar with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus*,
nevertheless there's many details to the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: Everybody who is familiar with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus* knows about the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*; **nevertheless there's many details to the tzimtzum and the reshimu**. It is not as simple as people think: "Ah, the light was there, and then He took it out, and now there was an empty place." It's not that simple.

phrases.en: you have to really cultivate a deep sensitivity for these ideas.

phrases.he: כי זהו עיקר היחוד האמיתי בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: because this, a proper understanding and really feeling the idea of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*, is the main thing, the main requisite for a true unification with *Atzmus Ein Sof*.
how everything is like nothing to Him.

phrases.he: גם בבחינת כללות כל ההשתלשלות דקו וכו'
phrases.en: even the whole totality of the *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*

blocks.text: There are two reasons to study these details and really think about them. First of all, the subject is very complex. Second, *lehaamik hadaas*: **you have to really cultivate a deep sensitivity for these ideas**, a very deep feeling and recognition for them. You should really be sensitive to it, really feel it, and not just understand it intellectually.

For this, a proper understanding and a real feeling for the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*, **is the main thing, the main requisite for a true unification with Atzmus Ein Sof**: to really connect everything in the world, and yourself, and see it all as a revelation of G-d, as part of *Atzmus Ein Sof*.

The main thing in that is to realize *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, **how everything is like nothing to Him**; how everything else is really nothing. It really is just G-d revealing Himself, and the reason this whole world looks like it is here is that He hides everything that He is except for this little thing, and this is like a little nothing.
Another side of *kula kamei k'la chashiv*: everything in the *hishtalshelus* is less than what is before it, and less to the point where it is infinitesimal, like nothing.

Anything you have in this world, you are going to say, "Ah, look at this. I have this great, yummy, triple chocolate fudge cake. It's so good. Mmm." Say, "No, that's like nothing." G-d has infinite fudge chocolate cake, not just triple fudge chocolate cake, and even more and more.

The good taste, the *geshmak* (relish), the chocolate and all the pleasure in it are really coming from a little *nitzotz* (spark), a little revelation of G-d that is in it. If you would get the full revelation, it would be so pleasurable that the soul would leave the body. "At least right now, without proper lenses and stuff."
blocks.title: Triple chocolate fudge cake

blocks.text: So when you look at anything, like a table, what it really is, is that G-d is hiding everything that He can do except for this table. And just making a table is like nothing compared to what He could really do.

By the way, there is also an explanation of *kula kamei k'la chashiv* in *nigleh* (the revealed Torah), "just a little interesting side": if you look in *Ein Yaakov*, the word is not *la* (not) but *k'la*, like *la*. And what is *la*? It is the name of the stuff that comes out from the sun, like a dust that the sun makes from scraping against its orbit or something. That is why during the day you cannot hear things from as far away: there is a background buzz from the sound of this *la* stuff. "So you know, that's interesting."

It is like the *mashal* of light: everything in the world is like light from the sun, and has no *metzius* (existence) of its own. Even at the level where you see it as its own *metzius*, it is like the photons that come out from the sun, the most ethereal, intangible substance, the least physical of the physical things, and their whole existence is to reveal what is coming from the essence, to reveal a light. It is the same idea.
blocks.title: The la that comes from the sun

blocks.text:
That is the way it is in *nigleh*, and this is the way we are explaining it in *Chassidus*. There are two things: *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, and *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him). *Kula kamei k'la chashiv* says the world is a *metzius*, but it is like nothing. *Ein od milvado* says there is no world.

It is not really a contradiction, because here we are saying that the world is still part of the revelation of G-d Himself. So it is a *metzius*, because G-d made it as a revelation of Himself; it is *mamash* a *metzius*, a revelation of Him. Only you should realize that the revelation you see in the *hishtalshelus* is just a little token example, and it is like nothing compared to the full revelation of G-d, if you would appreciate it.

**Even the whole totality of the hishtalshelus of the Kav** (the line of light): our whole world with all of the spiritual worlds, with heaven, the lower *Gan Eden* (paradise), the upper *Gan Eden*, and even higher, in *Atzilus*, even higher in *Adam Kadmon*, and even everything that is going to come with the revelations of *Moshiach*: all of these are like nothing.

Yes. Even when *Moshiach* comes, the thing that we want is not the external things of *Moshiach*, that we are going to have peace and tranquility and prosperity; really, even that is not what we want. And not even the revelations of G-dliness of *memalei kol almin* and *sovev kol almin* (the light that fills all worlds and the light that encompasses them); that is not what we want either. We want that when *Moshiach* comes, we are going to see G-d Himself.
blocks.question: "What do you mean? Even Moshiach is like nothing? The whole thing we want is Moshiach!"

blocks.text: This is what we say on *Shabbos*: *Ein aroch lecha Hashem Elokeinu ba'olam hazeh, v'ein zulas'cha malkeinu l'chayei ha'olam haba, efes bilt'cha go'aleinu limos haMoshiach, v'ein domeh lecha moshi'einu lis'chiyas hameisim*. In this world, in *Gan Eden*, in the time of *Moshiach* and in the World to Come, it is all worthless without G-d. *Efes bilt'cha*: it is nothing without You.

When a person realizes this, that everything he sees in the world, even the greatest spiritual revelations, is only a little token, symbolic thing, an external thing whose point is for you to see the *atzmus u'mahus* (the essence) behind it, the revelation of G-d, and not to see it as its own thing, then he is not going to want the *tafel*, the secondary external thing. He is going to want the real thing behind it.

You know what it is like otherwise? It is like a guy who gives you a check. The real thing you want is not the check; you want it to be backed, you want the money in the bank. Even a dollar bill: the paper and the artwork on it are worth something, but that is not what you want. You want the fact that it is backed by a promise of much more than what the paper is actually worth. If a big guy signs a check, just his signature is worth something, but that is not what you want. If he writes you out a million dollar check, you want the money.

So when a person looks at the world, he realizes it is like a check. The main thing is to cash it; the main thing is what is in the bank, and this is just a symbolic thing of giving it over to you. Then you are not going to want the world as its own thing, because you say that is like nothing. "So G-d gave us a check for infinite stuff, and we should, you know, cash it."
blocks.title: The check and the money in the bank

sections.title: Directing the will to the Essence alone: what is there for me in the heavens?
sections.summary: Understanding the *tzimtzum* lets a person aim his will, with *mesirus nefesh*, at *Atzmus Ein Sof* alone. Every revelation, even *sovev* before the *tzimtzum*, the heavens of the heavens, cannot contain Him, not even as a vessel for a vessel.

phrases.en: Until a person will be able to straighten out his desire

phrases.he: במסירת נפש לעצמות אור אין סוף לבדו
phrases.en: that he'll self-sacrifice just for the *Atzmus Ein Sof* itself

blocks.text:
**Until a person will be able to straighten out his desire**: when a person properly understands the *hishtalshelus* and the idea of the *tzimtzum*, he will not be distracted by other things. He will be able to look past them and see the real main thing, what is really important, and that is what he will want.

That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): **that he'll self-sacrifice just for the Atzmus Ein Sof itself**, willing to give up anything physical, and even spiritual, to connect to G-d Himself. He realizes that everything else is secondary and meaningless in itself, and its whole purpose is to connect to G-d. If you have that, you have everything.

The king gives people an opportunity to come to his treasure chamber and take whatever they want. But around it he sets up all kinds of booths, with food and people playing music and different distractions. People come and start partying; they figure they have so much time, they get distracted, and then it is too late.

So too, when a person comes into the world, *Hashem* sets up all these revelations to distract him. He gets dazzled by how great the physical things and the spiritual things are, and he can get distracted and go off after these side things.
blocks.title: The king's treasure chamber and the booths

blocks.text: *Lechaven* means to direct it straight. Like a laser pointer, or on a gun, where you have sights and you get them aimed and aligned properly: you get your sights on it and you are able to go straight. That is the idea: when a person understands the *tzimtzum*, he is able to aim his *ratzon* (will) properly.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אתה הוא יהו״ה לבדך,
phrases.en: like it says, you are *Hashem* alone,
that You, etc.

blocks.text:
**Like it says, you are Hashem alone.** It could mean that there is nothing else of value, but really it means there is nothing else at all; it is just G-d. Then we say, **that You, etc.** What is the "etc."? The continuation of the verse: that You made the heavens and the earth and everything in them, and that everything bows to You.

That means that really there is only G-d, and that *Hashem* made the world and everything in it is just part of His revelation. So you should realize that it is not its own thing. That is what it means that everything bows to You: everything is really *batel* (nullified) to *Hashem*.

phrases.en: And this is what it means: the King that is exalted alone, that He's above everything.

phrases.he: בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: this is the idea of *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שמתנשא גם מימות עולם דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: which is exalted over the days of the world of *Adam Kadmon*, meaning that it transcends even the limitations of *Adam Kadmon*,
this *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* is called *yemei kedem*.

blocks.text: **And this is what it means: the King that is exalted alone**: we call G-d the King who is above everything. **This is the idea of Malchus of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum.**

It **is exalted over the days of the world of Adam Kadmon**: it transcends even the limitations of *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is the general image of the final goal of the whole *hishtalshelus*, the way it is going to be when *Moshiach* comes. Even that, *Hashem* is really above. He just chose it as a little thing to represent the way we will connect to Him, and our *avoda* (divine service) is to try to do that.

**This Malchus of Ein Sof is called yemei kedem** (the days of old). Usually *Adam Kadmon* is called *yemei kedem*, but here he is talking about *Kadmon*; *yemei kedem* can refer to different things. Here he calls *Adam Kadmon* *yemos olam*, because there are two levels. *Yemos olam*, the days of the world, means the regular limitations of the *hishtalshelus*, or of whatever level you are talking about. *Yemei kedem* means the way those *middos* (attributes) are preceded in the *etzem*. But the *etzem* can really control them and do whatever it wants; it is not bound by them.
*Yemei kedem*: "that's like in the good old days, where, you know, he had to walk uphill both ways to school and stuff like that," where it is impossible.
So here he is talking about *Malchus*, the *middos*, the way they are in the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, which, as was said at the end of chapter 11, is called *yemei kedem*.

phrases.en: the heavens
the heavens represents the general *sovev*, the general encompassing light that's after the *tzimtzum*.
and the heavens of the heavens,
which is before the *tzimtzum*, which means the lights of the *tehiru ila'a*,
they cannot contain You.
it's not even a vessel for a vessel,
like it says that He engraved an engraving in the higher purity

blocks.text: This is **the heavens** of the verse, "The heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain You." What does it mean? **The heavens represents the general sovev, the general encompassing light that's after the tzimtzum**: the light that includes the whole *hishtalshelus* after the *tzimtzum*.

**And the heavens of the heavens, which is before the tzimtzum**, the lights of the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity): **they cannot contain You.** Everything in the *hishtalshelus*, even the lights before the *tzimtzum*, does not really capture G-d's essence. He is way higher than everything.

**It's not even a vessel for a vessel, like it says that He engraved an engraving in the higher purity.** What does it mean, a vessel for a vessel, an engraving for an engraving?

Say you have a diamond and you engrave letters into it, but you cannot really read them, because there is not enough contrast between the diamond and the letters. So what do you do? You press the diamond into wax, and in the wax you can see the letters that were really there in the diamond.

So too, the letters that were estimated in *Kadmon*, in the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), are still hidden, too fine to see the difference. That is why it says *glif glifu*, a double engraving. After the *tzimtzum* they are stamped out as on wax and revealed as something separate, and then you can really see the letters. That relationship, between what is after the *tzimtzum* and these letters, is called a *kli l'kli* (a vessel for a vessel), an engraving for an engraving.
blocks.title: The engraved diamond pressed into wax

blocks.text: That means that even though it is not revealed directly, it is revealed indirectly. But G-d's essence, G-d Himself, is not revealed even indirectly, even as a vessel for a vessel: nothing captures Him, even as a representation of what He really is.

He is really higher than everything. On the one hand, nothing can reveal Him. On the other hand, when He chooses to reveal Himself in something, the whole essence is there. But nothing can capture Him inherently. It is kind of like either you have it or you don't: to connect to G-d, you have to connect to Him directly, and when you connect to Him, you will be able to get it. But if you understand or appreciate even the highest revelations, they will not really capture Him, and you will not really appreciate Him.

phrases.en: And like it says, what is there for me in the heavens?

phrases.he: שהוא גם בחינת סובב הכללי שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: which includes even the general *sovev* that's before the *tzimtzum*,
which is called the heavens of the heavens.
And with You I desire nothing on the earth,

phrases.he: בבחינת קו וחוט בחינת ממלא הכללי כו'
phrases.en: the earth represents *memalei*, the way that G-d is revealed not in a transcending way, but in an individualized way in *hishtalshelus*, in the *hishtalshelus* of the *kav v'chut*.

blocks.text:
**And like it says, what is there for me in the heavens?** That **includes even the general sovev that's before the tzimtzum, which is called the heavens of the heavens.** What is there for me in the spiritual revelations, even the highest, encompassing things?

**And with You I desire nothing on the earth**: **the earth represents memalei** (filling), the way G-d is revealed not in a transcending way but in an individualized way, in the *hishtalshelus* of the *kav v'chut* (the line and the thread): in a measured way, revealed in *chachma* and *bina* and all the different things differently. Once you have G-d, you have everything, and if you do not have Him, it is all worthless.

The *Alter Rebbe* used to sometimes fall into a state of *dveikus* (cleaving to G-d), and he would roll on the floor and say, "I don't want Your *Gan Eden*, I don't want Your World to Come, I only want You alone." That is what he used to say in the earlier years.

In the later years, before his passing, he said: "I know the revelations of the lower *Gan Eden*, I know the revelations of the upper *Gan Eden*, I know the revelations of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, and I even know the essential revelations where *chachma* and *Asiya* are equal. But I give myself over with my whole power of *mesirus nefesh* so that You, *Hashem*, should listen to the prayer of every Jew as if he were a *tzaddik gamur* (a perfectly righteous man) davening on *Rosh Hashana*."
blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe: I only want You alone

blocks.text: "I don't know," says Rabbi Walters, "maybe" the point of that is that the highest *mesirus nefesh* is like it says in *HaYom Yom*: it is better to love whom *Hashem* loves than even to love *Hashem*. So in a way, even better than wanting G-d, which is still a kind of selfish thing, that you want to be connected to G-d, is that you should want Him to be good to His people. That is the importance of the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The tzimtzum in one point: the light hidden in itself so that a little can shine
sections.summary: There are many *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*, but they all come to one point: so that the infinite light can be drawn down in a measured way, as a *Kav*, G-d hid the revelation of Himself within Himself and let only a little shine, making a quantum leap from infinite to finite.

phrases.he: והנה יש כמה אופנים במשלים שונים להשכיל ביאור ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי
phrases.en: There are many different types and ways of *meshalim* to be able to understand, to get a concept of the *tzimtzum*, which is called the empty place,
as is known to somebody that goes into these things in depth.

blocks.text: "Now we're going to start explaining the *tzimtzum*, and then we'll explain the *reshimu*." **There are many different types and ways of meshalim** (analogies) **to be able to understand, to get a concept of the tzimtzum, which is called the empty place**, the *makom panui*, **as is known to somebody that goes into these things in depth.**

Why so many? In general the *tzimtzum* is a very simple, general *mashal*. But if you are going to really understand it properly, the deeper the idea is, the more *meshalim* you need, and they need to be different ways.

phrases.en: but the general idea of the *tzimtzum* comes to one main point.

phrases.he: והוא כדי שיוכל להיות אור אין סוף בבחינת השפעה בצמצום בבחינת קו,
phrases.en: that in order for the infinite light, the revelation of G-d, to be brought out in a limited way, in a measured, limited way, which is the idea of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: הוצרך לצמצם עצמות אורו שישאר בהעלם בעצמותו
phrases.en: G-d hid *atzmus oro*, He hid the revelation of Himself, so that it should remain hidden within Himself,
and it shouldn't all shine,
just a little bit of it,

phrases.he: כדי שיהיה אחר כך המשכות האור בדילוג הערך
phrases.en: And through this, that *Hashem* hides His *atzmus or* and just brings out a little bit, there could be a jump, a quantum leap in its *erech*, in its quality, in its degree.

blocks.text: With all these different *meshalim*, **the general idea of the tzimtzum comes to one main point**: **that in order for the infinite light, the revelation of G-d, to be brought out in a limited way, in a measured, limited way, which is the idea of the Kav** (the line), **G-d hid** *atzmus oro*, the essence of His light: **He hid the revelation of Himself, so that it should remain hidden within Himself.**

**And it shouldn't all shine, just a little bit of it.** And through this, that *Hashem* hides the essence of His light and brings out just a little bit, **there could be a jump, a quantum leap in its erech** (measure), **in its quality, in its degree**: so that it goes from being an infinite thing to a finite thing, from being a creator to a creation.

sections.title: The first mashal: the teacher boils a deep idea down to one point, and nothing is missing
sections.summary: A teacher hides the depth of his understanding and gives the student one point, but he has not forgotten the rest, and the short way includes all of it, as the *Mishna* includes the whole *Gemara*. So the *tzimtzum* is not literal: from the teacher's side and from the student's, it is all there.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמשל אור שכל עמוק ורחב שבעצמות המשפיע
phrases.en: This is like a *mashal* of a deep and broad subject within a teacher's brain,

phrases.he: שכדי שיומשך ממנו למקבל הבלתי ערך אליו,
phrases.en: in order for him to bring this idea over, to teach it to a student that is much lower than him, it's not comparable to him,

phrases.he: הוצרך המשפיע להעלים בעצמו כל עומק השגתו,
phrases.en: The teacher has to hide within himself the whole depth of his understanding.

phrases.he: ולא ישאר רק בחינת רושם, כנקודה א',
phrases.en: So he has to hide everything and only leave an impression like one little point of what he wants to say,
from the whole depth and the whole breadth with all the details,

blocks.text:
**This is like a mashal of a deep and broad subject within a teacher's brain.** **In order for him to bring this idea over, to teach it to a student that is much lower than him**, not comparable to him, **the teacher has to hide within himself the whole depth of his understanding.** He cannot teach the student the way he himself understands; it is too deep, the student will not understand, he will be confused.

**So he has to hide everything and only leave an impression like one little point of what he wants to say**, what he wants to explain, **from the whole depth and the whole breadth with all the details.** He has to boil it down to one little point.

A big math genius knows math with all its depth and all its different branches, which is the breadth: whole numbers and fractions, rational numbers and irrational numbers, trigonometry and calculus and advanced mathematics, "and all kinds of things that I don't know about at all. You know, they do like differential equations or something, and he knows them all."

Now he is going to teach math to a little kid, a two-year-old, three-year-old. How does he start? With one little point, a simple thing: one and one is two. That is really where math starts. But that is still too abstract; it is not complicated, but it is abstract. What is one and one? What do you mean? So he makes it even simpler: one fishy and one fishy are two fishies. "But we're not up to there, he didn't say that." Right now we are only saying that he brought it down to one little point that he is going to explain.
blocks.title: The math genius and the little kid

blocks.text: Einstein wrote a book about relativity that he says anybody can understand, and he gives an analogy there of somebody bouncing a ball on a train and somebody else standing on the ground next to the train. The person on the train sees it going straight up and down; the person on the ground sees it going up and down and forward, in these little rainbows. He has this whole thing, and he makes it much simpler.
blocks.title: Einstein's ball on the train

phrases.en: it's not like the depth and the width and the breadth of the idea go away completely.

phrases.he: רק כמו השונה בדרך קצרה, שכל העומק ורוחב הפלפול ישנו בשכלו,
phrases.en: it's not like he forgot about the rest of the details, but rather it's like somebody that's just saying something over in short, like a summary, that he has the whole depth and the whole width in his head.

blocks.text: Even though he takes the idea and distills it to one little point, **it's not like the depth and the width and the breadth of the idea go away completely.** **It's not like he forgot about the rest of the details, but rather it's like somebody that's just saying something over in short, like a summary, that he has the whole depth and the whole width in his head**, the whole *pilpul* (debate). **Just that it's now hidden within himself.** He still remembers it, he knows it, but right now he is not thinking about it, because **right now he's just saying the point in short**: the *kitzur*, the short way.

You ask somebody the *halacha*, and he tells you the *halacha*, the bottom line. Then you ask him why, and he starts explaining: "Oh, well, it's a whole thing. We learn it from the verses, and then it's explained like this, and then the *Gemara* is a dispute, and they rule like that, and then the *Rishonim*, and then the *Shulchan Aruch*, and the *Shach* and the *Taz*, and this whole thing, and finally we get to the *halacha*." He knows that whole *pilpul*, but he does not say it. He just tells you, "You can eat the chicken. It's kosher."
blocks.title: You can eat the chicken

blocks.text:
But if you are a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar) or something, and you want to know, and you ask him, "Why did you rule that way?", then he will explain; and the more you know, the more he will expand and explain, all the way back to the way he understands it.

**Just that in order for the recipient to understand this short way**, in order for the student to understand, **he has to make it short, and even for himself he just focuses on the point.**

Back in Europe, people would take a chicken to the *shochet* (slaughterer), the *shochet* would slaughter it, then they would bring it to the *dayan* (rabbinic judge) to check whether it was kosher, and then they would bring it home and salt it and finish koshering it. So all the time people would bring chickens to the *Rav*. Some lady brings a chicken to the *Rav* and asks if it is kosher. He starts telling her, "Well, the *Shach* says like this, and the *Taz* said like that." She does not want to know all that; she will be confused.
blocks.title: The chicken brought to the Rav

sensitivity.reason: The questioner is "some lady" who does not want the sources and "will be confused" by them; read alone it can sound condescending to women.

He starts telling him, "Well, the *Shach* says like this, and the *Taz* said like that." He does not want to know all that; he will be confused.

blocks.text: To be a good *Rav*, you have to just say the *halacha* clearly, as if that's it. That is what you are supposed to do. Even if you are giving them a lenient ruling, you are not supposed to make them feel that it is a *b'dieved* thing (acceptable only after the fact). You are supposed to say, "That's it, that's what you're supposed to do," that this is *l'chatchila* (the proper way from the start) what they are supposed to do. If you know they are poor and they cannot, so that's it, that's good.

Some people are not so good with that. You ask them a *halacha* and they start telling you, "Well, ah, not so simple, there's this, there's that, it's complicated," and you come away and you do not really know what the *halacha* is. That is not what you need to hear.

So too, if you start giving the student all this explanation, he will not even understand the point; he will not get what you are trying to say. You have to just tell him the point in very simple terms. **As is explained elsewhere at length.**

blocks.text: **And this that the idea is left like a little point, that's just a very short point**, like the little short notes you make for yourself, the short way that you tell the student: **it's not a true and complete tzimtzum.**

That would be **like somebody that completely hides the idea; then it would be totally missing to the mekabel** (the receiver). That is if the teacher decides, "You know what, this is too complicated for you, I'm not going to teach it to you," or that it is a secret and he is going to hide it. Then the student does not get it at all.

We are not talking about a teacher who decides not to tell the student something. We are talking about a teacher who is trying to explain the idea to the student, but cannot tell it to him the way he himself understands it. He has to explain it in a way the student will understand, so he has to make it short.

**So the idea is that when the teacher says this short, simple explanation for the student, the whole long idea is all hidden within that short explanation.** It is all there. **And he's not missing a point, and not even a half a point**: not even the little, minute details are missing. It is all there, so the student is really getting the full explanation.

phrases.he: כמו שכלול בדין הקצר שבמשנה כל האריכות הפלפול שבגמרא
phrases.en: just like how in the short *din* in the *Mishna* is included the whole *pilpul* in the *Gemara*.

phrases.he: וכמו שלא נעלם ליודע כל הפלפול גם בשעה ששונה לעצמו דרך קיצור
phrases.en: and just like for the teacher that knows the whole *pilpul*, it's not missing to him even when he teaches it in a short way,

phrases.he: שנמצא שידיעתו באריכות מקפת בהעלם כל התגלות הקיצור
phrases.en: So it comes out that his knowledge of the whole long explanation of the *Gemara* encompasses in a hidden way the whole revealed short explanation of the *Mishna*.

phrases.he: ולא שנסתלק לגמרי כשכחה וכהאי גוונא כו'
phrases.en: And it's not like it totally went away, that he forgot it.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב ביאור זה באריכות במקום אחר.

blocks.text: **Just like how in the short din** (law) **in the Mishna is included the whole pilpul in the Gemara.** If you analyze the *Mishna*, you will be able to extract the *Gemara* from it, because when Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi wrote down the *Mishna*, he really knew the *Gemara*. He knew the whole *pilpul* of why we say it; that is the main thing of the *Gemara*.

It was not exactly our *Gemara*, with those different *Amoraim* and so on, but the points the *Gemara* brings up, why the *halacha* is this way and why it is that way, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi knew. When he wrote the *Mishna*, he picked the cases very carefully, chose the wording carefully and put them in a certain order. Each *din* he chose is not just telling you a law: it teaches a general case, a certain rule, a principle. If you analyze them, compare and contrast them, and look at the order and the examples he chose, it all teaches you different *chiddushim* (new insights). From that you see the common denominator and the difference, you extrapolate the reasoning, and you can reconstruct the whole *Gemara*. That is what the *Amoraim* did: they were taught by their teachers how to learn the *Mishna*, extracted the whole *Gemara* from it again, and wrote it down.

**And just like for the teacher that knows the whole pilpul, it's not missing to him even when he teaches it in a short way.** When Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi wrote down the *Mishna* as notes, and when he looked in it, he saw the whole *pilpul* of the *Gemara* there. **So it comes out that his knowledge of the whole long explanation of the Gemara encompasses in a hidden way the whole revealed short explanation of the Mishna. And it's not like it totally went away, that he forgot it.** No, he knows it, and he sees it in this short explanation.

So too for the student: it is all there, and the student is really getting the full explanation; he just does not realize it yet. When he studies and thinks about it and develops his mind, he will slowly appreciate more and more of what he was taught, until he realizes everything, just like the teacher.

So in this *mashal* of the teacher and the student there are two main things. The main theme is that you need the *tzimtzum*, but the *tzimtzum* is not literal. What does that mean? Even though the teacher hides most of his intellect when he teaches the student and gives over only one little point, the whole understanding is not really missing; it did not really go away. That is so both from the teacher's point of view and from the student's.

From the teacher's side there are two things. One, the teacher did not forget it, so if you ask him, he will be able to explain it to you. Two, even when the teacher looks at the short explanation, he sees the whole thing there; he sees how that short explanation really explained everything. If you told the teacher that short explanation, he would understand the whole thing; you would not even have to explain it to him.

For the student there are also two things. Even though right now he is getting only one little short explanation, he is not really missing the rest, because whatever he is able to understand, the teacher explains to him. As soon as he is ready, he has a question, he wants to know something else, he just asks, and he gets it. And not only is it really there in the teacher, whom he can ask, but even in the little explanation he got: even if the teacher goes away, if he studies what the teacher told him, he will be able to get everything, because it was really all there.

So from the teacher's side and from the student's side, it is there, both in the teacher's mind and in the explanation. The only difference is that the student does not appreciate it all yet, because he has a small mind; as he develops, he will be able to see everything like the teacher. That is the first, the main *mashal* for the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The second mashal: the soul holds back to live in the body, yet stays whole
sections.summary: To become the life of the body the soul hides most of what it can do, since the two are not comparable. Yet the whole soul is bound to that small light and feels what the body feels, like a plant tied to the earth's power of growth; and when a limb is lost, nothing is lost to the soul.

phrases.en: the second main type of *mashal*.
the consciousness of the soul in the body.

phrases.he: גם כן עולה על דרך הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it also comes to a similar conclusion, similar point as the previous *mashal*.

blocks.text: Now **the second main type of mashal.** The first main *mashal* is from a teacher and a student. The second main *mashal* for the *tzimtzum* is **the consciousness of the soul in the body**, and **it also comes to a similar conclusion, similar point as the previous mashal.**

phrases.he: והוא בהיות שכדי שישתנה מחיי רוחניים שבעצם הנפש לחיי בשר, הוצרך להיות בחינת העלם וכיווץ האור של הנפש בתחלה
phrases.en: in order for the soul to come into the body, the soul has to hide its full potential,
because there is no comparison between the two.

blocks.text: Again, just as with the teacher and the student, where the teacher has to hide the way he understands the idea in all its depth because it is too much for the student, too complex and too broad: so too, **in order for the soul to come into the body, the soul has to hide its full potential**, because the soul can really do a lot more than the body can do. It could see a lot more than the body can see and understand a lot more than the body can understand.

A person who is dreaming sees all kinds of things, or a person hallucinates. But when the soul comes into the body we say to it, "Hey, you know, easy there. We want you to only see what the eyes see."

Sometimes you could be sitting in class, the teacher is talking, and instead of listening to the teacher or even seeing him, your imagination wanders off, and you are seeing and hearing a whole other world, in a different place. That is just going from the eye to the brain. If you go up to the soul it would be even more, even more unlimited. But we do not want that to happen. We want your soul to keep quiet, and only when light hits your eye, to see what your eyes are seeing. Or else there is no point in being in the body.
blocks.title: Daydreaming in class

blocks.text: So in order for the soul to come into the body it has to say: "Okay, I'm going to put aside everything that I can do, everything I can see and feel, and I'll be quiet, and I'll wait, and only see something when light hits the eye, and only hear something when air hits my ear." The soul does that automatically, because it wants to come into the body. A person who really wants to can sometimes go out of the body a little bit, but then he will not be able to see and hear.

Once the Rebbe Rashab was saying a *maamar* (a Chassidic discourse), and some people were making noise in the side room. Since his whole desire was to teach *Chassidus* and the noise was disturbing that, he automatically shut off the ear that faced that room, so that it would not hear. It was done unconsciously. Later they realized he could not hear out of one of his ears; they did not know what had happened, then they realized it was from that, and he turned it back on. His soul had decided it did not want to be in the ear anymore, so it left.
blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's ear

blocks.text: Or in *dveikus* the soul goes up, and then it is not receptive; it is seeing things in higher levels, kind of like a dream. That is one step up. Higher still is *nevua* (prophecy). A prophet totally loses his physical senses when he is getting a prophecy, except for Moshe, who could stand face to face, as if talking to a regular person. The regular prophets were even called crazy people when they had a prophecy: they would fall on the ground and totally lose their senses, unable to see or hear anything around them, because the soul was going out of the body a little bit. So in order for the soul to come into the body, it has to limit itself and be revealed only according to the body.

**Because there is no comparison between the two.** The body is not a good recipient for the soul; it is too small to hold the real light of the soul. So the soul has to hide its true potential, at least at first.

phrases.en: nevertheless,
The soul is affected by what happens to the body, the soul itself.

phrases.he: אם כן גם אור הגשמת החיות תתחבר ונקשר אל אור עצמותה הרוחני
phrases.en: Even though the light of the soul is coming into the physical life, when a person sees something or feels something, it is connected to and tied to the essential light of the soul.

phrases.he: כצמיחה גשמית שנקשר בכח הצומח הרוחני כו'
phrases.en: Like the physical growth of a plant, that even though there's just a little plant, it's connected to the spiritual power of growth.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, the soul is affected by what happens to the body, the soul itself.** It is not that a little ray of the soul comes into the body while the soul remains aloof. A little ray of the soul comes into the body, but the whole soul is attached to it.

**Even though the light of the soul is coming into the physical life**, when a person sees or feels something, **it is connected to and tied to the essential light of the soul.** So if you hit somebody, his soul feels the pain. If you hurt or insult somebody, it can hurt him all the way to his essence, the core of his being, because it is not really his body that is feeling it. It is not just some little biological thing that sends an impulse; his whole soul feels it. So too with happiness: when he gets happy or has pleasure from something, the whole soul gets excited and has pleasure from it.

**Like the physical growth of a plant, that even though there's just a little plant, it's connected to the spiritual power of growth.** "It's like very metaphorical": a little tree or plant has just a thin little stem connected to the ground, and the earth is a huge, massive potential for growth. This stem is one little example of it, one little possibility, siphoning out a little drop. Even the little drop that comes through the stem is filtered by the roots, to take up only the parts this plant can use. Different plants use different nutrients; that is why they rotate crops, because some use certain parts and others use other parts. It goes according to the seed and the DNA of the plant, bringing out one little possibility of what the earth can bring out. But if you disconnect it from the source, the source of everything, it will not grow anymore. So it is connected constantly to the whole source.
blocks.title: The thin stem and the whole earth

blocks.text: In the same way, if the whole soul were not in the body, the body would not be able to see or hear or feel. You need the soul to be there, or else the person would not be alive.

phrases.en: but when a limb of the body is, G-d forbid, cut off,

phrases.he: לא יחסר באור וחיות רוחניות של אבר זה
phrases.en: it will not detract from the light and the spiritual life force, spiritual consciousness of this limb.
and the proof is
from a blind person that is able to give birth to someone that can see.
as is known,

blocks.text: That is the one side: we see that on the one hand it is only a little, only a *tzimtzum*, only a little bit of it, and yet the whole essence is there. Now the other side.

**But when a limb of the body is, G-d forbid, cut off, it will not detract from the light and the spiritual life force, spiritual consciousness of this limb.** Even though the whole essence of the soul is connected to the body, it is not trapped there. If you hurt the body, it will not hurt the soul.

**And the proof is from a blind person that is able to give birth to someone that can see**: his child will be able to see. If his soul were missing the power of sight, he could not give it over, because the power of reproduction makes something like you. That is why people give birth to people, animals to animals and plants to plants: you reproduce something like you, with a certain minimal variation.

If somebody, G-d forbid, had his eye gouged out, and that meant his soul no longer had the power of sight, it would be as if the soul were made up of different powers and you took one away: now this is a creature with only the other powers. From then on it would be a new species of people that do not see. But that is not the way it is.
Even physically, even in the spiritual side of the physical, the DNA, they still have the letters, the potential of sight; it just has to be brought out into actuality in a healthy eye.

Even when the DNA gets messed up: "I don't know exactly how it works," says Rabbi Walters, but they tried with fruit flies to make wingless fruit flies. With genetic engineering and breeding they made them have smaller and smaller wings, defective wings, and tried to get rid of them. They would get closer and closer to not having wings, more and more mutated, and then after a few times they would revert to perfectly healthy flies: the next generations would suddenly be totally normal again. Something in the way it is set up, the soul, forces it to follow a certain form and keeps it from departing from it too much. **As is known.**
blocks.title: The wingless fruit flies

phrases.he: אין זה רק שהרוחניות הוא בהעלם,
phrases.en: Because the spiritual power is still there in a hidden way.

phrases.he: וישנו במציאותו, חופף על חיות הגשמי שבגוף
phrases.en: and it exists in its totality, in its perfect state, hovering over the physical life force of the body.
it's called the form of man.

phrases.he: והיינו על דרך הנזכר לעיל בידיעה שבהעלם כו'
phrases.en: and this is like the knowledge of the teacher that is hidden in his short explanation.
and all of this is explained elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: Why can a blind person give birth to a child that can see? **Because the spiritual power is still there in a hidden way, and it exists in its totality, in its perfect state, hovering over the physical life force of the body.** And **it's called the form of man**, the *tzelem*: the soul has a spiritual form that hovers over the body and makes the body go the way it is supposed to go.

You even see this a little with a phantom limb: when somebody loses a limb, he can still feel it sometimes, because as far as the consciousness in his brain goes he feels that hand, only the hand is not there. That is still somewhat a physical thing, but for sure as far as the soul goes, as in a dream, he can have the whole thing.

**And this is like the knowledge of the teacher that is hidden in his short explanation.** From the teacher's point of view it is all there, and really from the student's point of view too. So too from the soul's point of view it is all there: it has the whole life force, and it really still has the power of sight, or whatever power was lost. And even the body really has the whole thing, as in the DNA; it is just hidden.

More than that: in the *mashal* of the short explanation the whole depth is really there. So too the body could really reveal the whole light of the soul. It just needs to be refined until it is able to reveal it.
At the time of *techiyas hameisim* (the resurrection of the dead), when *Moshiach* comes, the body will be refined enough to reveal the whole light of the soul.

That, by the way, is why people do not live forever now. Right now it is painful for the soul to be in the body, because it cannot express its whole essence there. So it does not want to stay; after a while it gets sick of it and starts to pull out, and the body starts to go down until the person dies.

But if the whole essence of the soul came into the body, and its whole *ratzon* were to be in the body, it could grow back the whole body even from one little part of it, the way it is going to be with the *luz* bone at *techiyas hameisim*. You see it with a child: when a child is born, the whole child develops very quickly from one little cell, two little cells. The body could really do that all the time, if the soul came into it all the way.
blocks.title: Why people don't live forever

blocks.text: **And all of this is explained elsewhere at length.** Those are the two main *meshalim*. Now he says quickly that there are also a few other *meshalim* like this.

So far the *tzimtzum* has been explained with two main *meshalim*. A teacher teaching a deep idea to children puts aside the way he understands it in his mind and leaves a simple explanation, like the *Mishna* to the *Gemara*. From the teacher's point of view he does not forget the idea, and he sees the whole depth in the explanation; and the student too receives the whole depth, length and width of the idea in the explanation, only he does not appreciate what he is seeing. That is the main *mashal*. And the soul coming into the body: the essence of the soul is connected to the body, so a person is affected by what happens to his body, and nevertheless if a part of the body is injured, it does not detract from the soul. "So now we're going to explain the *reshimu*."

sections.title: More meshalim: the power of movement and the genius in one idea
sections.summary: The power of movement contracts into one movement and the genius into one idea, yet each stays bound to its source: the body moves only with the soul, and in one idea you see the whole genius. One-way: the source gives life to the detail, but the detail does not capture the source.

phrases.he: וכן כח התנועה הרוחניות כשבאה בתנועת הגשם, מתצמצמת בעצמותה כו'
phrases.en: So too, when you move, the spiritual power of movement has to be limited severely in order to come and make a particular movement.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה התנועה גשמית מחוברת ומקושרת בתנועה הרוחנית
phrases.en: Nevertheless, the physical movement has to be connected to the spiritual movement, or else it won't move.

blocks.text: **So too, when you move, the spiritual power of movement has to be limited severely in order to come and make a particular movement.** The whole power of movement is not revealed, because it is infinite; it can make so many movements, and now it is coming into just one movement.

**Nevertheless, the physical movement has to be connected to the spiritual movement, or else it won't move.** "Like I said, dead dogs don't bark." If the whole essence of the soul were not there, the body would not be able to move.

But the movement does not really capture the soul. If you just move the body, that will not make the body alive. "Like Frankenstein wouldn't work": the whole idea was that if you make electricity go through the body, it can make the body move. But that is just the physical side; it would not give the body life. As was said before, the whole essence of the soul connects to the body, but it is not trapped there.

It is a one-way thing, "like a square is a rectangle, but a rectangle isn't a square." The soul comes into the body, and its whole essence is connected there, but if you have the body you do not have the soul. If you have the soul, the body will be able to move; if you do not have the soul, the body will not be able to move. But even if you move the body, that will not capture the life of the soul.

phrases.en: and so too with other types of *meshalim*,

phrases.he: כמו ענין התחכמות שכל פרטי מכח המשכיל שלו ששורה עליו בהעלם כו'.
phrases.en: like when a person comes up with a particular idea, the person's whole genius is really expressed in that one idea.

blocks.text: **And so too with other types of meshalim, like when a person comes up with a particular idea, the person's whole genius is really expressed in that one idea.** Nevertheless, the idea does not capture his whole genius. If he were not such a great genius he could not have come up with it; but if you understand what he said, you will not be a genius like him.

Only he could come up with the idea. But for his genius to come up with this particular idea, he has to limit it and bring it out in one very limited way. Nevertheless, he still has his whole power of intellect: he could come up with another idea, with any idea, and he knows it. And on the other hand, if you look at this one idea, you see not just the idea but the genius, and you see that he could really come up with any idea.

Not only that: if you really study what he wrote or said, it will start to make you smart like him. You will start to think like him, until you are able to come up with ideas like he can. That is the idea of *osios haRav* (the teacher's letters): the letters themselves, not the idea but the way he said it, have his way of thinking hidden in them.

By the way, that is what is said about the *Mishna*. The wisdom of the *Mishna*, the way they understood and thought, was so much greater than the way we think; it is really a G-dly intellect, not even humanly possible to think that way. So what do you do? It says that if you study *Mishnayos* a hundred times, the angel of the *Mishna* comes down and teaches it to you, and then you understand it. That means that when you keep going over the letters and the ideas of the *Mishnayos*, it sets up your brain to think like the *Mishnayos*. Every review filters your brain more and reinforces those patterns and that way of thinking, until you get the way the *Tannaim* thought, and then you understand it.

That is the way it is with anything. It says that if you learn a *maamar* sixty times, you get the *etzem*: "Then you *chap atzmus*" (grasp the essence).

sections.title: The reshimu: an impression, like a blueprint or a mnemonic, from which the whole can be drawn
sections.summary: A *reshimu* is an impression: the original is gone, nothing of the light is left, yet what was there can be drawn out of it. The craftsman's marks and a sign made to remember hide the intellect more than the *Mishna* hides the *Gemara*, since the *Mishna* still speaks of the same thing.

phrases.en: however, in order to understand the *reshimu*,
that the idea of a *reshimu*, of an impression, implies that everything was removed to be hidden,

phrases.he: ולא נשאר מהכל רק רושם כו'

blocks.text: **However, in order to understand the reshimu**: *reshimu* literally means an impression. Like in those detective movies where the guy has a pad of paper, writes a phone number on it and rips it off, and the other guy comes and rubs a pencil over the pad and sees what it was. The original piece of paper is gone, but there is an impression left. People think *reshimu* means a residue. It doesn't. It means the original thing is completely gone, but you can figure out what was there from an impression that is left; like a footprint, or a fingerprint, which is kind of like a residue, but things like that.
The idea of a *reshimu*, of an impression, **implies that everything was removed to be hidden, and nothing is left, just an impression, but none of the original light is left.**

phrases.he: הוא מובן יותר מענינים משלים אחרים,
phrases.en: so the *reshimu* is better understood by different *meshalim* than we said until now.
for example, a blueprint.

phrases.he: שיוכל לעשות הבנין בקיצור קו זה שברושם, שכולל כל אריכות המעשה בקיצור רושם זה
phrases.en: You're able to take the blueprint, and you're able to build the whole thing.

blocks.text: **So the reshimu is better understood by different meshalim than we said until now.** "Till now we gave like five *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*, now we're going to give five for the *reshimu*."

The *roshem* (mark) the craftsman makes is, **for example, a blueprint. You're able to take the blueprint, and you're able to build the whole thing.** Say you are building a skyscraper: you can take the blueprint and just follow it and build the whole thing, or a whole house. The same with any craftsman: if they are making a new *aron kodesh* (ark) out of woodwork, they first draw it to figure out where everything goes, and then they make it; a silversmith making *Kiddush* cups first draws out the design.
blocks.title: The craftsman's blueprint

blocks.text: But here it is not talking about just a drawing; that would be different. It is a blueprint: a few lines and symbols and marks. To a normal person they would not necessarily say anything, but if you know how to read a blueprint, you will be able to build the entire thing from it. Not necessarily exactly a blueprint, but certain marks, a shorthand notation used to mark the dimensions. So the first *mashal* is a craftsman's notes. There are no actual instructions for making the building or whatever he is making, and no actual picture of it; there is no manifest explanation there at all. You would have to know how to do it.

As he is going to say in a moment, the *Mishna* still relates to what the *Gemara* spoke about. The *Gemara* talks about somebody's cow that gores somebody else's cow: what do you pay, who has to pay whom, what if it was the first time, the second time, the third time, what if it was in the sun, all these different things. The *Mishna* is also talking about that; it just has much less about it. Anybody who learns *Mishnayos* will have a general knowledge of Jewish law and be somewhat familiar with the ideas in the *halacha*. Maybe he will not know the whole thing or understand it well, or appreciate the real depth, why these cases were chosen and not others, but he understands what is going on. Even without explanation, you get the basic idea of what the *Gemara* was talking about.

A person who looks at a blueprint, if nobody explains it to him, is not going to understand. There the intellect, the idea of how to build this thing, is completely hidden. It is there, but it is completely hidden.

blocks.text: **Or like somebody that makes a sign to help him remember**, like tying a string around his finger. The string has nothing to do with what you are actually trying to remember. A person who looks at it is not going to study it and figure out what the other person wanted to remember.

**The sign has nothing to do with the actual thing you're trying to remember, it's just to help you remember**, **like it says in the Gemara, you should make mnemonics for yourself.** Like a mnemonic, "Roy G. Biv" for the colors of the rainbow: nobody is going to look at that and figure out what it is, even though it is there, hinted there. In a way it is more than the string on the finger, because there is something there that represents everything. Or the one for the planets: "My very eager mother just served us nine juicy pickles." If you just heard the mnemonic, you would have no idea what it is talking about; but once you know, it helps you remember.

So these are the first two *meshalim* of the *reshimu*.

sections.title: Deeper concealments: the thrown stone, the hand sign and the writing finger
sections.summary: In the thrown stone the force is severed from the thrower yet carries his whole power; in a hand sign and in the moving fingers of a writer the intellect is hidden further still, until it reappears on the paper. All the *meshalim* of the *reshimu* make one point: the essence is hidden, yet all of it is included in the impression.

phrases.en: there's another type of *mashal* for the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שהוא מורה ענין הצמצום וההעלם הרבה יותר
phrases.en: which reveals a much deeper type of a concealment within the *reshimu*, a different aspect of the *reshimu*.
this is like somebody that throws a stone.

phrases.he: שכח המוליך אותו נבדל מן העצם
phrases.en: that the force that's carrying the stone is severed from him.

blocks.text: **There's another type of mashal for the reshimu, which reveals a much deeper type of a concealment within the reshimu, a different aspect of the reshimu.** **This is like somebody that throws a stone**: **the force that's carrying the stone is severed from him.**

In class, a kid throws a paper airplane or a spitball, and then he goes like this, everybody is sitting like that, and you don't know who did it. Why don't you know? Because once he throws it, the force he put into it is severed from him. He can go back to rest, he does not have to move his arm, he can go back to sitting there looking in his book, and you cannot see the connection between the thing and who did it. Both in the object that was thrown you no longer see the connection to the person, and the person can rest: they are separate.
blocks.title: The spitball in class

phrases.he: ועם כל זה כל כח התנועה מלובש בו בהעלם
phrases.en: but nevertheless, even though you don't see the connection anymore between the person and the stone or whatever it was he threw, his entire power of movement is in there; that's what's moving it.

phrases.he: אך שהוא בריחוק נבדל ביותר מכחו העצמי שבידו
phrases.en: but the force that's in the stone is very distant and it's completely separate from the force of his hand.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כח התנועה עצמה שמניעה בעצמו בגשם שמלובש בגלוי בגשם ביותר כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: On the other hand, if somebody actually holds something and moves it, then you see the connection between the person's power of movement and the thing that he's moving.

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, even though you don't see the connection anymore between the person and the stone or whatever it was he threw, his entire power of movement is in there; that's what's moving it**: his strength, and also his desire. Really his whole essence is there, and that is why he is responsible for what happens. If somebody throws a stone and it damages property, or if it kills somebody, he could actually be killed. That means his soul is held accountable: his whole essence is responsible for what is going on with this stone.

**But the force that's in the stone is very distant and it's completely separate from the force of his hand.** **On the other hand, if somebody actually holds something and moves it, then you see the connection between the person's power of movement and the thing that he's moving**; it is much more manifest. When you throw something, you put some energy into it, which is in a way a *reshimu*: you leave just an impression of your force in it, and then you can go back to rest, and it carries the thing.

It is the same with all of these. With the blueprint, the engineer or architect puts the instructions for building the building into the blueprint, and then he can walk away. He can give it to somebody else, and they can build it: "If they know how to read a blueprint, the guy can die, nobody cares, they can build it." That idea is really there in all the *meshalim*.

phrases.he: ויש בחינת העלם יותר גם מזה,
phrases.en: the *reshimu* has even more of a concealment than this,
this *mashal* is similar to the *mashal* of the mnemonic.

phrases.he: והוא כמו הרומז בידו לאיזה שכל עמוק ביותר
phrases.en: this is like a person that hints with a hand motion to a very deep idea.
the physical movement is totally detached from the idea.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה מבין השכל מתוכו כו'
phrases.en: Nevertheless, even though it's just a motion, just a hand movement, a person understands the intellect within it if you know what it represents.

blocks.text: And **the reshimu has even more of a concealment than this**, which we see from a different *mashal*; **this mashal is similar to the mashal of the mnemonic.**

**This is like a person that hints with a hand motion to a very deep idea.** Like this, see this? There is a whole philosophy: the whole hippie philosophy is represented by these two fingers, but it is just a hand movement. Or when the Rebbe would go like this: there was a whole thing that was understood there, of not being *nifal* (swayed), going against everything and doing whatever you have to do with determination. You say, "Well, what's that?" It is just a motion.
blocks.title: The peace sign and the Rebbe's gesture

blocks.text:
**The physical movement is totally detached from the idea.** A person once took his intellect, expressed it and connected it to this motion. Once that was done, nobody has to think anymore to put content into the motion; it has already been thrown. Nobody is creatively coming up with this peace sign.

**Nevertheless, even though it's just a motion, just a hand movement**, you would say, "What does that have to do with intellect? So what's a guy waving fingers in my face?" Nevertheless **a person understands the intellect within it, if you know what it represents.**

phrases.en: and even more than this,

phrases.he: העלם אור השכל בתנועת האצבע בכתיבתו אותו

phrases.en: explained elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: **And even more than this** is the concealment of the light of the intellect in the movement of the finger when one writes. When you are writing, you can be writing the deepest ideas, but what comes out in your hand is just moving your fingers like this. The advantage of this *mashal* is that it is even more hidden: neither you nor somebody else who is looking sees the intellect in the motions of your fingers. The only way you see it is that it comes out again on the paper. When it comes onto the paper, then you see: oh, there was an intellect. It just passes through.

Really you can put all these *meshalim* together, and this book itself is the *mashal*. The Mitteler Rebbe took this deep idea, G-d and the whole *hishtalshelus* and how G-d creates the world, and made it real short and simple, just 80 pages, with all these little *meshalim*. Then he wrote it down, and then he threw it. It went from Russia to America, and into the future, 200 years in the future, and landed here, and now we are learning it. In a way it is detached from him: he just did it, and we don't see the Mitteler Rebbe walking around anymore. Nevertheless, we say that this is his book and he is responsible. That is why in the beginning he writes that he should be forgiven for any mistakes: because he is responsible for the way we understand his book. It is as if he is sitting behind the book and teaching it to us.
blocks.title: The book thrown two hundred years

phrases.he: והכל עולה לסגנון א' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: but all of these *meshalim* of the *reshimu* are really the same general point:
that the essence remains hidden, that the original light is gone, is hidden completely.
but even though it's hidden, it's all included within this *reshimu* or this point.

blocks.text: **But all of these meshalim of the reshimu are really the same general point: that the essence remains hidden, that the original light is gone, is hidden completely**; **but even though it's hidden, it's all included within this reshimu or this point.** So really it is all there. On the one hand it is completely hidden, you do not see it at all; and yet it is all there, because you see that you can pull it all out.

Really he gives five *meshalim*, or six, and they are not all for the same thing; they never use the same *mashal* for the same thing. Why he gives all these *meshalim* is explained in a *maamar* in *Ateres*, where the Rebbe Rashab explains it, and in a letter of the Rebbe about it. The main idea is that it keeps being more hidden. "If you want to look up exactly what, you can see the *maamar*."

All the *meshalim* show how hidden the *reshimu* is, with two main points. One is that the idea, the intellect, is completely hidden, and yet you can pull it out. The other is that it becomes separate, something far away. That has two sides. It becomes detached from the essence, so you do not see the connection. And it is a *shinui hamahus* (a change of its nature): it does not look like an intellect anymore, just a motion, or a sign to remember something, a mnemonic; even a blueprint looks like a few little squiggles and notes, and you do not see the instructions for building a building there. And it can be thrown: the original person can leave, and it is completely self-sufficient, so to speak.

"I think," says Rabbi Walters, this last *mashal*, the writing, is an introduction to the idea of the *Kav*. Just as at the end of 13 he gives the *mashal* of the growth, which seems to be an introduction to the relationship between the *tzimtzum* and the light before the *tzimtzum*, so here: the question we are going to ask in chapter 14 is how you can pull the light out of the *reshimu*. If it is completely hidden there like a point, how can it come out? In the *mashal* of the writing, the intellect becomes more and more completely hidden, until it is like a point in the person's moving fingers with no revelation of intellect at all; but when it comes onto the paper, it becomes revealed again. "And we'll discuss how that works later."

reviewQuestions.question: Why is this tzimtzum called the first, when there are tzimtzumim before it?
How do kula kamei k'la chashiv and ein od milvado differ, and why is there no contradiction between them?
What does it mean that even the heavens of the heavens are not a vessel for a vessel, and what is the mashal of the diamond and the wax?
In the mashal of the teacher and the student, in what ways is the whole idea still there, from the teacher's side and from the student's?
How does a blind parent's seeing child show that the soul loses nothing when the body is injured?
Why is the blueprint a greater concealment than the Mishna, and the writing finger greater still?
